Subject: Hosting trajectory & legacy cluster offboarding — recap and next steps

Hi Ryan / Priya — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our call + clear next steps so we all have alignment.

Key notes from the call:
- Current stack: Helix runs model training and inference on an on-prem legacy GPU cluster ("oldcluster-01") and thin integrations to a third-party LLM API (BigBlueAI) for peak loads.
- Primary concerns: PHI isolation, network egress restrictions, and predictable 99th pct latency under 250ms for inference.
- Preference expressed: leaning to Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) for throughput predictability but need to validate VPC peering and KMS/HSM compatibility for keys.
- Migration blockers: data ingress constraints from legacy cluster, prompt/kvcache warm-up strategies, and billing model alignment for token-heavy pipelines.

Proposed next steps:
1) Vivek / Infra team to outline Dedicated vs Private (VPC) checklist focused on networking & key management (timeline: 2 business days).
2) Marissa to provide a ballpark estimate for a 3-month Dedicated pilot + optional burst credits. (attached: estimate draft)
3) Helix to send security questionnaire items we didn’t cover (Priya) — we’ll return answers + SOC2 scope sample.
4) Technical POC scope: run 1 model on Dedicated with a small traffic mirror from oldcluster to validate latency and KV-cache warm-up (target start week of Nov 30).

Attachments: estimate_dedicated_capacity_20261121.xlsx (pricing draft)

If that looks right, can we lock in a 30-min POC kickoff next week? I’ll propose slots separately.

Thanks,

Thanks Lauren — quick clarifications from our side: 
- We are indeed leaning Dedicated for the pilot. The main gating items are: (1) support for customer-managed KMS keys (HSM) and (2) VPC peering with strict egress rules (no public internet from inference nodes).
- Compliance: we need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a data retention policy that allows us to set TTLs for KV cache (we can’t persist PHI beyond 24 hours).
- Migration note: our in-house infra serializes model context differently; cold start token overhead was ~30% on our last test. We want to validate cache priming strategy with realistic traffic.

If Redwood can meet the KMS/HSM and VPC requirements, we’ll sign up for the 3-month Dedicated trial and run the POC. Priya will be our procurement contact — she’ll coordinate any PO/SOW questions.

—Ryan

Ryan — thanks for the clear asks. Short answers + proposed technical POC scope below.

KMS/HSM & encryption:
- We support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and can extend to HSM-backed key stores in Private deployments. For Dedicated we offer envelope encryption where private keys are customer-provided and rotated per your policy.

VPC & networking:
- Dedicated nodes can be deployed in a VPC with static egress endpoints; we support VPC peering and private IP routes (no public egress). We’ll provide a network diagram and ACL checklist.

SOC2 & data retention:
- Can share our SOC2 report redacted for procurement. KV cache TTLs are configurable; for the POC we’ll configure a 24-hour TTL and demonstrate no persistence outside ephemeral RAM.

Migration / cache warm-up:
- POC plan (technical):
  * Mirror a small percentage (~1%) of live traffic from oldcluster to Redwood Dedicated.
  * Run a 48-hour warm-up with scripted priming prompts to measure token overhead and 99th pct latency.
  * Provide tracing hooks so your SREs can correlate requests.

Target success criteria for the POC:
- 99th pct latency < 250ms for 95% of validation traces
- Token overhead within 10% of baseline after warm-up
- KV-cache TTL enforced and validated via trace logs

Timeline:
- Network + KMS checklist delivered by Redwood: 2 business days after sign-off
- POC kickoff (integration + mirror): aim week of Nov 30

I’ll attach a short ops playbook and a sample comp/quantization profile to help your infra team evaluate memory/latency tradeoffs.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Infra & Customer Solutions
